A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same EM-based preference-alignment framework despite its renaming. Their main texts, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original alignment experiments, hyperparameter ablations, and controlled synthetic-noise experiments estimating annotator reliability.

after.justification: v3 retains original experiments and adds MultiPref evaluations, robust-baseline comparisons, confidence analyses, and measured training times.

M1.justification: The posterior weighting, policy objective, reliability updates, and mini-batch EM procedure remain unchanged under the RE-PO name. Table 1 corrects the written SimPO and CPO losses by replacing repeated winning-response terms with losing-response terms. These are limited objective-formula corrections; the PDFs do not establish corresponding implementation changes.

E1.justification: v3 adds training and evaluation using MultiPref, with 227 identifiable human annotators and genuine disagreement, substantially extending coverage beyond the original virtual-annotator and synthetic-noise settings. UltraFeedback and AlpacaEval 2 remain. Arena-Hard remains in the ablation, although its main comparison results are removed.

E2.justification: v3 Table 2 adds evaluated rDPO and Hölder-DPO baselines and label-smoothing variants of all four objective families. v1 evaluated only the standard DPO, IPO, SimPO, and CPO methods against their robust counterparts and the base models. ROPO is newly discussed but is not an evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: New supplementary protocols include MultiPref rescoring with DeepSeek-V3.2-Exp, a reliability-initialization grid of 0.80/0.90/0.95/0.99, and wall-clock comparisons with matched optimization settings and no concurrent jobs. The original benchmark metrics, ablation grid, and synthetic-noise procedures are retained. These additions do not establish changed settings for the retained experiments.

E4.justification: v3 adds annotator-reliability distributions across backbones and initializations, two low-confidence preference case studies, evaluator-sensitivity testing, and computational-overhead analysis in Appendices E–H. These examine denoising behavior, dependence on initialization and judge choice, and computational cost. The original hyperparameter ablation and synthetic-noise verification remain.

E5.justification: v3 Table 8 first reports training-time means and standard deviations over three seeds; v1 supplies no repeated-run counts or uncertainty estimates. Benchmark win rates still lack such reporting. Figure 3 additionally summarizes variation across annotators, which is distinct from uncertainty across experimental runs.

E6.justification: The original AlpacaEval scores, retained ablation values, and Figure 2 curves are unchanged. v3 adds baseline, MultiPref, alternate-judge, confidence, and runtime results, while removing the main Arena-Hard comparison. Newly reported label smoothing exceeds RE-PO for Mistral CPO (28.5/28.8 versus 27.6/27.8 LC/WR) and Llama SimPO LC (48.1 versus 46.9). The Llama IPO LC gain is corrected from +3.3 to +4.7 without changing its underlying scores.

T1.justification: The Gibbs-model and EM derivations and calibrated-model convergence guarantee are retained. The fixed-point lemma and convergence proof are consolidated into Theorem 4.1 and Appendix D, rather than replaced by a new guarantee. Limited formal changes include the corrected loss expressions in Table 1 and omission of v1 Remark E.1 explicitly demonstrating nonidentifiability when all preference probabilities equal one-half.

C1.justification: v1 explicitly targets collective consensus and treats legitimate preference pluralism as noise; v3 narrows the stated problem to recovering noise-free preferences from corrupted annotations. The abstract and introduction also withdraw the headline Arena-Hard improvement claim and emphasize AlpacaEval 2. The general-framework contribution and conditional convergence claim remain.

C2.justification: v3 adds a substantive failure condition: a highly misaligned initial model can confidently reinforce incorrect labels, limiting applicability beyond the ideal calibration assumption. It newly interprets reliability histograms, case studies, and robust-baseline comparisons as denoising evidence. Conversely, v1's explanations that stronger backbones and certain standard losses benefit more are removed.

D1.justification: v3 removes v1's implementation paragraph specifying TRL, full-parameter tuning, DeepSpeed ZeRO-3, one training epoch, the cosine schedule, learning rate 5×10^-7, batch size 64, and DPO temperature 0.01. Appendix H adds timing controls and hardware information, and Appendix I adds a MultiPref access link. These additions do not restore the missing training recipe or establish actual configuration changes.

R1.justification: v3 adds Liang et al.'s ROPO and Miranda et al.'s MultiPref references, while removing the Berlin/Bakker pluralism references and tooling citations. The iterative robust-training/filtering discussion is reassigned from ORPO/Hong to ROPO/Liang, and RE-PO is positioned as complementary to other noise-handling methods. The broader alignment and noisy-label literature remains largely the same.

P1.justification: The abstract, substantial portions of the introduction and related work, and the main-results discussion are rewritten. Terminology changes throughout from RPO to RE-PO, the experimental narrative gains a dedicated MultiPref subsection, and the theoretical presentation consolidates the lemma and theorem. The extent of rewriting exceeds a simple rename or local copyediting.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redrawn, and Table 2 is reorganized from paired method rows with explicit gains into standard/label-smoothing/RE-PO columns. v3 adds the MultiPref tables, eight-panel reliability histogram, two case-study tables, and runtime table. The original ablation is renumbered, and Figure 2 retains its plotted evidence with revised labeling and captions.

improvement.justification: Real multi-annotator evaluation and comparisons against explicit robustness alternatives strengthen evidence that v1 lacked, while the calibration discussion clarifies a meaningful failure condition. However, v3 removes key reproduction settings and the main Arena-Hard comparison. Its runtime summary also conflicts with Table 8: SimPO overhead is approximately 32–40%, exceeding the claimed roughly 20% bound. These tradeoffs limit the net quality gain.
